# dn-ioc

> Small, zero-dependency TypeScript dependency-injection kernel. A provider is a factory function. No decorators, reflection, runtime dependencies, or global container.

- **Runtime:** ESM-only. TypeScript requires `"moduleResolution": "bundler"` (`NodeNext` / `Node16` unsupported). Uses no platform APIs (`process`, DOM, timers); runs identically on Node.js, Bun, Deno, browsers, workers, and edge runtimes.
- **Install:** `npm install dn-ioc` | `pnpm add dn-ioc` | `yarn add dn-ioc` | `bun add dn-ioc` | `deno add npm:dn-ioc` (or direct `import ... from 'npm:dn-ioc'`).
- **Browser CDN:** `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dn-ioc` or `https://unpkg.com/dn-ioc` (`index.min.js`), or `https://esm.sh/dn-ioc`. Append a version tag in production to pin a release.
- **Links:** Human reference: https://dn-ioc.lyz.cloud/ — Repository: https://github.com/MunMunMiao/dn-ioc

## Constraints (Do Not Invent)

- Does **not** have: decorators, reflection, a global container, modules, request-scoped containers, multi-bindings, or OS/browser signal listeners.
- `stop()` does **not** await unfinished detached factories, cancel their I/O, or revoke already-held JS references. Request admission, cancellation (`AbortController`), and graceful drain stay in application code.
- Handles from `token`, `provide`, `provideFor`, and `bundleProviders` are frozen opaque objects tracked by identity. Copied/cloned objects are rejected. Trusted in-process kernel, not a sandbox.

## Public API

```ts
// 6 runtime functions
function token<T>(description?: string): Token<T>
function provide<T>(factory: Factory<T>, options?: ProviderOptions): Ref<T>
function provideFor<T>(key: InjectKey<T>, factory: Factory<T>, options?: ProviderOptions): ProviderDef<T>
function bundleProviders(...inputs: ProviderInput[]): ProviderBundle
function isProvideRef(value: unknown): value is Ref<unknown>
function bootstrapApp(fn: BootstrapAppFn, options?: BootstrapAppOptions): App

// 15 exported types
interface Token<T> { readonly [TOKEN_TYPE]: T }
interface Ref<T> extends Token<T> { readonly [REF_TYPE]: true }
interface ProviderDef<T> { readonly [PROVIDER_DEF_TYPE]: T }
interface ProviderBundle { readonly [PROVIDER_BUNDLE_TYPE]: true }
type RefType<T> = T extends Ref<infer U> ? U : never
type InjectKey<T> = Token<T> | Ref<T>
type ProviderInput = Ref<unknown> | ProviderDef<unknown> | ProviderBundle | readonly ProviderInput[]
type ProviderOptions = { providers?: readonly ProviderInput[] }
type InjectFn = <T>(key: InjectKey<T>) => T
type OnDisposeFn = (fn: () => void | Promise<void>) => void
interface Context { inject: InjectFn; onDispose: OnDisposeFn }
type Factory<T> = (ctx: Context) => T
type BootstrapAppFn = (ctx: Context) => void | Promise<void>
interface BootstrapAppOptions { providers?: readonly ProviderInput[] }
interface App extends AsyncDisposable { start(): Promise<void>; stop(): Promise<void> }
```

- `isProvideRef(v)` returns `true` only for an authentic `Ref` from `provide()` (false for tokens, bindings, bundles, copies).
- `BootstrapAppFn` must return `void | Promise<void>` (wires and runs the graph; does not return a value).

## Resolution & Scoping

- **`bootstrapApp()` is lazy:** Builds the root scope and validates root `providers` immediately, runs no factories. `start()` runs the root factory once, is idempotent (returns the same `Promise`), and rejects if already stopped.
- **`Ref<T>` vs `Token<T>`:**
  - `Ref<T>` (`provide()`) carries a default factory and self-installs on first `inject()` in the active scope. Not a global singleton: list shared/stateful refs in bootstrap `providers` so sibling subtrees share one instance.
  - `Token<T>` (`token()`) has no default and must be bound via `provideFor()`. Use `description` for diagnostics (`No provider for token: Name`); unnamed tokens and anonymous arrow factories report `<anonymous>`.
- **Scope lookup & caching:** Searches active scope up to root. Instances cache on their owning scope, or on their private child scope when the provider declares nested `providers`.
- **Private subtrees (`options.providers`):** Visible only to that provider and its descendants; sibling subtrees stay isolated. Nested inputs are validated on first resolution of that subtree.
- **Parent-owned consumers:** A consumer installed/bound in a parent scope resolves its dependencies in that parent scope. Overriding a dependency in a child scope does **not** rewire a parent-bound consumer; rebind both consumer and dependency in the child scope when both must change.
- **Snapshots & precedence:** Provider arrays/bundles are snapshotted at creation time (later array mutations have no effect) and flattened in source order. Duplicate keys in the same scope: **later binding silently wins** (including nested `providers`).
- **Async factories:** `inject()` returns sync values directly and a shared `Promise` for async factories. A rejected async factory is evicted from cache so a later `inject()` can retry while running. Put `Promise<...>` in async token types: `token<Promise<Settings>>('Settings')`.
- **Startup scope:** `start()` tracks only Promises returned or awaited by the root factory; unawaited fire-and-forget Promises are not part of startup.

## Lifecycle & Cleanup

- Call `stop()` only when something outlives the graph (servers, DB pools, timers, tests, unmounted browser sub-apps). Short-lived scripts and full-page browser graphs do not need it.
- `stop()` synchronously closes `inject()` app-wide (even for cached instances and private subtrees), then awaits `onDispose` hooks newest-first (LIFO). **Capture needed dependencies into local variables before calling `onDispose()`.**
- `onDispose` is callable only while its factory is running and before `stop()`. Hooks must return `void | Promise<void>` (wrap non-void calls like `{ server.close() }`). Never `await app.stop()` inside a hook (deadlocks).
- Repeated/concurrent `stop()` calls share one `Promise` and run each hook once. All hooks run even if one fails: single failure rethrows unchanged; multiple failures throw `AggregateError('App stop failed')`.
- `start()` failure automatically runs `stop()` before rejecting (combined failures throw `AggregateError('App startup and stop failed')`). Successful `start()` and post-start runtime errors never auto-stop the app.
- `App` implements `AsyncDisposable` (`Symbol.asyncDispose` + `Symbol.for('Symbol.asyncDispose')`) for `await using app = bootstrapApp(...)`.
- Wire shutdown yourself: `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` (Node/Bun), `Deno.addSignalListener` (Deno), framework unmount (browser sub-apps), or synchronous-only `pagehide` hooks (`navigator.sendBeacon`) for tab unload.

## Layered Architecture & Testing

Import direction decides `Ref` vs `Token`:
- **MVC (inward/downward imports):** Layers import the layer below → use `Ref` (`provide()`). List stateful/connection refs in bootstrap `providers` to share one instance.
- **DDD / Clean Architecture (inverted imports):** `domain/` declares interfaces + `token()` ports (imports no other project layer); `application/` uses `provide()` and injects domain tokens; `infra/` imports `domain/`, binds adapters with `provideFor()`, and exports one `bundleProviders(...)`; entrypoints (`main.ts`) install the bundle once.
- Never export a DDD adapter as a `Ref` imported by `domain/` or `application/` (creates an outward dependency / module cycle). Adding a new adapter is two edits in `infra/`: its `provideFor()` + one entry in the bundle.
- Inject entry dependencies inside the root factory so missing bindings reject `start()` instead of failing mid-request. Enforce layer import rules with Biome or ESLint.
- **Testing:** `provideFor()` overrides both refs and tokens identically.
  - Unit tests: install only fakes. Missing token fake fails fast (`No provider for token: Name`); missing ref fake silently builds the real ref.
  - Integration tests: list real bundle **first**, overrides **after**: `[infraProviders, provideFor(orderRepositoryToken, fake)]`.
  - Name tokens after their interface; assign an arrow factory to a named `const` (`const OrderService = (ctx: Context) => ...; provide(OrderService)`) when you want readable cycle traces instead of `<anonymous>`.

## Exact Runtime Errors

- `No provider for token: Name` — unbound token
- `Circular dependency detected: A -> B -> A` — sync or async cycle
- `Invalid inject key received` — non-handle or copied object passed to `inject()` / `provideFor()`
- `Invalid provider input received` — invalid entry in `providers` (thrown synchronously by `bootstrapApp()` for root inputs, or on subtree first `inject()`)
- `Cannot inject after the app has stopped` — `inject()` after `stop()` (checked before cache or key validation)
- `onDispose can only be called while the factory is running` — `onDispose()` called after factory returns/settles
- `Cannot register cleanup after the app has stopped` — `onDispose()` called after `stop()`
- `Cannot start an app that has been stopped` — `start()` called after `stop()`

## Minimal Example

```ts
import { bootstrapApp, provide } from 'dn-ioc'

const configRef = provide(() => ({ greeting: 'hello' }))
const greeterRef = provide(({ inject }) => {
  const config = inject(configRef)
  return { greet: (name: string) => `${config.greeting}, ${name}` }
})

const app = bootstrapApp(({ inject }) => {
  console.log(inject(greeterRef).greet('world'))
})

await app.start()
```
